S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is characterized by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and a distorted perception of body weight or shape or undue influence of weight/shape on self-evaluation. Patients often deny the seriousness of their low body weight and may present with rigid rules around food, compulsive exercise, or other weight-control behaviors. Onset is typically in adolescence or young adulthood but can occur later in life, often in the context of perfectionism, need for control, or precipitating stressors around body image, health, or life transitions. It is distinguished from other eating disorders by the combination of underweight status with cognitive overvaluation of thinness and active restriction, rather than recurrent binge/purge episodes at normal or high weight as seen in bulimia nervosa or binge-eating disorder.

patient.personality: Detail-oriented and highly disciplined, Detrail is a routine-driven, competitive worker who takes pride in self-sufficiency and mentoring others while quietly holding himself to very high standards.
patient.stressor: Detrail’s preoccupation with physical conditioning began when his company shifted contracts to a large luxury complex, where he found himself constantly interacting with upscale tenants and younger, visibly fit maintenance techs he was now supervising. Around the same time, a minor back strain from lifting an HVAC unit led his employer’s occupational health provider to warn him about his weight and "longevity" in this physically demanding role, which he internalized as a threat to his career plans of becoming a facilities manager and eventually launching his own firm. His meticulous, all-or-nothing temperament translated into increasingly rigid rules around eating and training, initially framed as a disciplined "cut" to be leaner and more agile for work and basketball, but gradually crowding out his enjoyment of food and social meals he used to cook for friends and mentees. Over months, he kept tightening these routines despite coworkers and mentees commenting that he looked "too run down," and he finally agreed to psychiatric evaluation after an occupational health visit flagged his markedly low weight and recommended he address the underlying beliefs driving his extreme pursuit of leanness.
patient.chief_complaint: “They keep telling me I’m way too thin for my job, and now work says I need to get checked out because my weight’s gotten so low.”

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: These days I pretty much live on black coffee, a protein shake, and maybe some chicken or egg whites at night, and if I feel like I ate too much the day before I’ll just skip a meal or two and tell the guys I’m too busy to stop for lunch on site.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: I know the scale at occupational health said I’m down a lot, and my pants are hanging off me and my hard hat strap is loose, but in my head it still feels like I’ve got extra I need to strip off to be as lean and sharp as the younger techs.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If I even think about eating something like pizza in the breakroom, I get this rush of panic that one slice is going to stick to me and I’ll balloon up and lose my edge at work, so I just shut it down and grab more water instead.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: When I look in the mirror before work, all I see is this soft belly and wide face that I swear everyone on the job can see, and I tell myself if I can’t get that under control I don’t deserve to move up to being a facilities manager like I’ve planned.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.
S084.manifestation: My girlfriend, my mom, and the company doctor all keep saying I look sick and worn out and that my heart could be at risk, but honestly I just think they’re overreacting because I can still outwork most of the crew and run the stairs at the complex without stopping.
